backlogged.summary: checkEntry only recognises a check whose first word is the runner. Leading env assignments (`FOO=1 node test/tool.mjs`) and `cd x && node ...` get no entry rule, so a new entry script run this way is still overlaid on base and can be judged vacuous. The contract excludes second commands, but the env-prefix form is not documented as unsupported.

Each distinct withheld entry creates one more base git worktree (addBaseWorktree plus a full overlay). A contract with many new-tool criteria adds worktree setup cost, and the worktrees are created lazily and cleaned up only at the end of verify.

F16 vacuity tests were rewritten to route through a base-side runner (`run.mjs`) so the new-test-file overlay still applies. This is necessary under the new rule, but it changes the shape of the existing F16 fixtures. The original direct `node test/math.test.mjs` shape is now covered only by the F42 tests.

checkEntry resolves the entry path relative to where the check runs, but overlay/newOnBase paths are relative to the git top. When the project (.harness dir) is a subdirectory of the repository, the two can differ and the entry rule silently does not apply (fails safe: the old behaviour). This is not described or tested.
checkEntry normalizes 'node test/x/..' to 'test', a directory. It is harmless because it never matches an overlaid file, but the parser could reject paths that normalize to a directory-like result.
A separate base worktree is created for each distinct withheld entry. A contract with many new-entry criteria multiplies worktree creation and disk use, and nothing bounds it.
